subject: Logic
title: Boltzmann Brain
description: A quick win: understand Boltzmann Brain.

hook.text: What if you're a brain that randomly assembled from cosmic chaos a second ago, complete with fake memories?

buildup.text: In an infinite universe, random fluctuations could assemble any structure—including a conscious brain.

discovery.text: Ludwig Boltzmann's statistical mechanics implies such brains might vastly outnumber evolved ones across infinite time.

twist.text: If Boltzmann Brains are more common, you're statistically more likely to be one than a real evolved being.

climax.text: Physicists take this seriously—some cosmological models are rejected specifically because they predict too many.

punchline.text: A universe that makes too many fake observers can't be right.

quiz.question: Why do physicists care about Boltzmann Brains?
options: Models predicting too many suggest the model is wrong
They prove the universe is random
